nodes.Question: Help us understand what works! *Comments or thoughts on the shared village spaces? 🌱*
nodes.Answer: I have generally positive thoughts about the shared village spaces, and I really appreciate how functional and comfortable they are to use. The layout is well-designed, practical, and makes it easy to sit down with a laptop to work, relax with friends, or cook and prepare meals. Cooking here is surprisingly enjoyable, and the open setup creates a very social and welcoming atmosphere. I also really like the overall design — the colors, the layout, the furniture and decorations — everything feels modern, friendly and pleasant to spend time in. One of the biggest advantages for me is the atmosphere of the space, with games and common areas that make it easy to connect with others, hang out, and enjoy time together. It’s definitely one of the things that makes the village feel alive and community-driven. However, I sometimes notice issues related more to how people use the space rather than the space itself. After bigger gatherings or parties the shared areas can get quite dirty, and fairly often I find myself cleaning up after others to make the place comfortable to use again. It’s not really a fault of the village, but it does impact the experience. Another challenge is the limited number of laundry baskets and kitchen items — many people take them to their rooms and don’t return them, which means there are fewer available for everyone else. It would be helpful to have more baskets or a system that encourages items to be returned after use. The same happens sometimes with dishes and utensils, so increasing the quantity could balance this problem. In general, I love the idea of the shared spaces — the functionality, the atmosphere, the possibility to work, cook, socialize or simply relax. The space itself works extremely well, and I enjoy spending time there. The main issues come from how some people treat it rather than from the space itself, and with a bit more responsibility or more shared items available, the experience could be even better. Overall, I think the shared village areas are a strong part of the community and a place with great potential, and I genuinely appreciate being able to use them.

So if i find it hard to focus on studying right next to my fridge i know i can always go and sit somewhere else. In the summer the area is also super good, for example close to islamds brygge and the lakes and not too far from central cph on the bike! I also enjoy that there are many social activities, but i am not forced to go to them, which makes me feel like it is more my own choice to join in on social things here

nodes.Question: Optional - why did you give your apartment this rating? 🛋️
nodes.Answer: The (single) cooking plate from IKEA is overheating - meaning if I cook something, it boils over when using 4 out of 9 heating settings (not specifically my plate but used and heard from multiple others). Then the entrance door is not enclosed correctly, so the hallway and thus our rooms & bathroom get super cold. Even after maintenance checked it, it’s still bringing in cold air and now we can barely open and close the entrance door. The common kitchen has barely any equipment and people steal constantly. Maybe use locks and a rental system/mandatory payment for new kitchen equipment which is locked and tracked, or worst case cameras (we did that in a previous dorm). People also generally don’t clean after themselves in the community areas. Lastly, having two (!!) vacuums for the whole village of 360 villagers is just unreasonable. Also because they keep being gone for way longer than 1h and often I find both in the same laundromat. Might make sense to just paint it according to the colour. Lastly, I know the washing machines are handled by a third party service, but the prices are outrageous. I have a dust allergy so I need to wash ca twice a week, and I can’t even add my laundry disinfectant, the “allergy” washing cycle doesn’t help either. Generally not the greatest living environment if I’m being honest, there’s much better places for the total price (considering needing to buy your own vacuum, own ladder, laundry prices and constantly rebuying kitchen appliances bc they’ve been stolen in the kitchen). Otherwise it’s a super nice idea of having a real community, and I understand some things are out of your hands. But hopefully you can implement some of these suggestions:))

nodes.Question: Last question! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿
nodes.Answer:
Overall, my stay here has been a really positive experience, and I genuinely appreciate the thought and care that has gone into creating the environment. It’s a place where it’s easy to feel comfortable, productive and socially connected. The shared spaces, the atmosphere, the design, and the opportunities to interact with others all contribute to the feeling of being part of a community rather than just living in a building. I value that a lot, and I think it’s something that makes this place unique.
 
 If I could suggest anything for improvement, it would mainly relate to encouraging residents to take a bit more responsibility for shared areas and shared items. The space itself works incredibly well — but it reaches its full potential only when everyone uses it respectfully. Small changes like increasing the availability of shared equipment, or reminding people to return dishes or laundry baskets so that others can use them, could make a noticeable difference. Apart from that, everything feels well thought out, functional and supportive of both individual and social life.
 
 Thank you for giving me the opportunity to share feedback — I’m happy to participate and I appreciate the chance to contribute to making this place even better in the future.

nodes.Answer: I rated the apartment 7/10 mainly because I genuinely appreciate many aspects of the place, especially its location, layout, and day-to-day functionality. The area is very convenient and well-connected, which makes living here practical and comfortable. I like that I have easy access to transportation, shops, and different services, so I don’t need to spend extra time on basic errands or commuting. The surrounding neighborhood feels pleasant, reasonably quiet, and generally safe, and I enjoy the atmosphere here — it strikes a nice balance between calm and urban convenience. This was one of the strongest factors influencing my score. I also value the functionality of the apartment itself. The space is laid out in a way that makes everyday living smooth and efficient. It’s easy to organize the rooms, move around, cook, rest, and work without feeling restricted. I appreciate that the apartment has what I need on a daily basis, and the interior feels practical and comfortable enough to spend time in. It’s definitely a place where I can settle into a routine without too much effort, which is something I consider important. At the same time, the reason I didn’t give a higher rating is because I believe there are still a few areas that could be improved or refined to make the space feel even better. Although I’m overall happy with the experience, I think with small upgrades or improvements — whether related to comfort, equipment, design, or general upkeep — the apartment could easily become even more enjoyable to live in. My rating reflects the balance of positive qualities and a bit of room for enhancement. So overall, I am satisfied and have had a good experience living here, mainly because of the location, practicality, and general usability of the apartment. I gave it a 7/10 because it meets my needs well, but I also see potential for it to become even better with some adjustments or improvements.
